stem: A 17-year-old learner driver has chronic weekday sleep restriction and daytime fatigue; which consequence of poor sleep is most important to highlight at this visit?
explanation: Driving accidents are a key consequence of poor sleep in adolescents. In a learner driver, daytime fatigue has immediate safety implications and should be specifically addressed.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because poor sleep increases the risk of driving accidents, especially in a fatigued learner driver.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because earlier pubertal timing is not a recognised consequence of poor sleep.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because primary hypothyroidism is not a consequence of poor sleep.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because neutropenia is not associated with poor sleep.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because progressive hearing loss is not a consequence of poor sleep.
